A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dual Goal Representations by the same authors and contain complete main texts and Appendices A–D. Their readable text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Lights Out experiments, OGBench evaluations, robustness tests and ablations in Section 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the learning curves in Figures 3–4 and evaluations in Tables 1–7.

M1.justification: The inner-product embeddings, goal-conditioned IQL training and downstream policy-learning procedure remain unchanged. v2's Equations 3–4 repeat losses already in v1's Algorithm 1; the practical reward was already specified in Appendix D.2.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 4x5 and 4x6 Lights Out puzzles, 13 state-based and seven pixel-based OGBench tasks, and noisy-goal scenarios.

E2.justification: Original, VIB, VIP, TRA and BYOL-γ remain the comparators in the corresponding benchmark tables, with the same GCIVL, CRL and GCFBC downstream algorithms. Newly cited successor-representation methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Training budgets, network configurations, evaluation episode counts, checkpoint averaging and noise settings remain identical in Appendix D and Tables 8–9. Moving the reward explanation into Section 4 does not change the existing -1/0 reward setting.

E4.justification: Both retain the early-versus-late fusion comparison, noisy-goal robustness test, aggregation-function ablation and direct-policy-extraction comparison (Tables 3–5 and Figure 4). The added antmaze explanation provides interpretation rather than a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both specify eight random seeds for Table 1 and four for other tables and plots unless stated otherwise. Standard deviations in tables and 95% confidence intervals in plots are retained.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–7 and plotted curves in Figures 3–4 are unchanged. Section 4 newly states that -1/0 rewards work better in practice than 0/1 rewards; v1's Appendix D.2 only specified the choice. This adds a limited qualitative finding without numerical results or comparison details.

T1.justification: Ex-BCMP is renamed BCMP, but the formal model, disjoint observation-support assumption, reward definition, theorem conclusions and Appendix A proofs remain unchanged. The newly displayed losses and reward identities restate mathematics already present in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and closing remarks retain the same claims about sufficiency, noise invariance, compatibility with existing GCRL algorithms and empirical benefits across 20 OGBench tasks.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 adds an antmaze example distinguishing position information useful for goal representations from joint-angle information needed for control. This refines the explanation for using a separate, more expressive downstream value function. Existing visual-puzzle limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices B and D retain the implementation, encoder, gradient-flow, sampling, hyperparameter and code-access information. The reward details move from Appendix D.2 to Section 4; the added loss displays repeat Algorithm 1 rather than disclose a new implementation.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a comparison with successor representations/features and four associated references, plus Steccanella and Jonsson (2022). Section 2 adds Du et al. (2019). These additions modestly expand coverage and clarify the distinction between optimal temporal distances and fixed-policy successor representations.

P1.justification: Localized revisions expand Section 4, relocate the reward explanation, replace 'heads' with 'embeddings' and Ex-BCMP with BCMP, and add related-work and explanatory passages. The section hierarchy remains intact, while the header changes from preprint to ICLR 2026 publication.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from page 6 to page 7, and Table 1 moves from page 7 to page 8. Added loss-equation displays and adjusted spacing reflow several pages. Existing figure graphics, table structures and captions are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the practical method easier to follow by integrating the reward transformation and existing losses into Section 4. The successor-representation comparison and control-information example also improve context and explanation. These are limited gains: numerical evidence and proofs remain unchanged, and the new reward-preference statement is unquantified.
